guard_patterns.handling: Keep gas and CO2e units explicit.
Keep operator and site identities distinct.
Keep provisional and final values distinct.
Keep direct and indirect scopes distinct.
Keep modelled and measured values distinct.
Do not infer zero from missing records.
Do not silently mix factor years.

packages.title: DESNZ 2026 activity-based conversion-factor scope QA
facts: DESNZ published 2026 greenhouse-gas conversion factors on 11 June 2026 for reporting UK activities in 2026.
Inputs include fuel volume, purchased electricity in kWh and distance travelled, with Scope 1, 2 and 3 treated separately.
The publication provides a full set, an automatic-processing flat file, methodology and major-changes documentation.
The factors support UK organisations and UK operations of international organisations.
Conversion factors calculate emissions from activity data and are not direct parcel measurements.

packages.title: DESNZ 2026 conversion-factor version and method guard QA
facts: The government updates the conversion-factor set annually and directs regular users to review annual changes.
Company-reporting activity factors differ from Defra spend-based multipliers used mainly for demand and supply-chain estimation.
Users are instructed to report the accounting method they use.
The voluntary-compliance statement describes the factors as a calculation tool rather than statistics in themselves.
Factor year and calculation method must remain explicit and must not be silently mixed.

packages.title: DESNZ conversion-factor NAEI and QA-governance QA
facts: The 2026 factors are based primarily on the National Atmospheric Emissions Inventory, compiled under IPCC 2006 Guidelines.
The inventory is updated annually with the latest available data and reviewed by the National Inventory Steering Committee.
The inventory is also subject to international expert review processes.
Conversion-factor method improvements use internal QA, peer review and steering-group oversight.
Strong national QA improves authority but does not provide parcel geometry or parcel attribution.

packages.title: Defra PRTR operator-reported industrial-data validation QA
facts: Defra published the 2024 UK PRTR dataset on 30 June 2026.
Covered facilities report annual pollutant releases to air, water and soil and specified off-site transfers.
Operators submit PRTR data to regulators, which cross-check permits, inspections and monitoring information.
Validation includes checks for omissions, errors and incomplete information.
A PRTR facility record strengthens site evidence but does not prove parcel ownership or total parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: Defra PRTR measured/calculated/estimated method-code QA
facts: UK PRTR guidance distinguishes calculation, measurement, estimated and unspecified reporting methods.
Measurement codes include ISO/CEN, permit-prescribed and weighing methods; calculation codes cover several prescribed or other methods.
E denotes estimated and U denotes unspecified in the PRTR method coding.
Reported quantities should retain their method code because measured, calculated and estimated values do not imply identical precision.
Missing PRTR data must not be interpreted as zero emissions for a site or parcel.

packages.title: UK ETS verified reporting and surrender obligations QA
facts: Covered UK ETS installation and aircraft operators submit verified previous-year emissions reports by 31 March.
Covered operators surrender sufficient UK allowances by 30 April for the previous scheme year.
The UK ETS replaced UK participation in the EU ETS from 1 January 2021, subject to stated Northern Ireland arrangements.
Verified ETS reporting is strong evidence within the scheme boundary but does not cover every possible site emission.
ETS operator, installation, scheme year and parcel geometry must remain separate evidence fields.

packages.title: UK ETS installation threshold and scope-boundary QA
facts: UK ETS covers specified regulated activities producing greenhouse-gas emissions.
Combustion coverage generally includes sites above 20 MW total rated thermal input, subject to the guidance's exceptions.
Northern Ireland electricity generators remain in the EU ETS under the stated arrangements.
Separate treatment exists for hospital or small emitters, so scheme coverage is not a census of all emitting sites.
Threshold or permit evidence is a candidate-quality signal, not parcel-level emissions evidence.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime 2026 start-date boundary QA
facts: Domestic maritime entered the UK ETS from 1 July 2026 and offshore vessels are scheduled from 1 January 2027.
Covered maritime operators must use monitoring plans and submit verified annual emissions reports.
The guidance sets scheme-specific surrender timing for the 2026 and 2027 maritime years.
The July 2026 scheme start must not be back-applied to 2024 inventory or local-authority data.
Maritime reporting is transport-activity evidence and not a fixed parcel measurement.

packages.title: ONS territorial, residence and footprint basis-boundary QA
facts: ONS identifies three UK greenhouse-gas measures: territorial, residence and footprint.
Territorial covers emissions inside UK borders and supports UK-wide targets.
Residence covers UK residents and UK-registered businesses and aligns with National Accounts.
Footprint covers supply-chain emissions for UK consumption, including imports and excluding exported UK production.
The three measures are valid for different purposes and must not be interchanged or converted to parcel values without explicit evidence.

packages.title: ONS latest cross-basis headline-value QA
facts: ONS reports estimated 2025 territorial emissions of 367 MtCO2e, 54% below 1990.
ONS reports provisionally estimated 2024 residence emissions of 478 MtCO2e, 42% below 1990.
ONS reports 2023 footprint emissions of 699 MtCO2e, 24% below 1990.
For 2023 ONS reports 384 MtCO2e territorial and 480 MtCO2e residence emissions.
ONS notes that previous-year estimates can be revised as underlying data and methods improve.

packages.title: NAEI 2026 greenhouse-gas dataset versioning QA
facts: NAEI lists a 2026 UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory covering 1990 to 2024.
The catalogue separately lists a 2026 source pivot table and country inventories covering 1990 to 2024.
Publication year and covered emissions years are distinct provenance fields.
NAEI separately catalogues national tables, point-source, gridded and map products.
Dataset-version metadata strengthens provenance but does not establish parcel-specific emissions.

packages.title: NAEI point-source, gridded and local-map product boundary QA
facts: NAEI treats point-source emissions, gridded emissions, UK emissions maps and local-authority maps as separate products.
Point-source records, grid estimates and local aggregates are different spatial evidence classes.
A grid-cell value must not be presented as a measured installation value.
A local-authority aggregate must not be presented as a point-source or parcel measurement.
Parcel binding requires geometry and attribution evidence beyond the NAEI product class.

packages.title: DfT 2024 domestic-transport mode-split QA
facts: DfT reports 110.4 MtCO2e from domestic transport in 2024, equal to 30% of total UK domestic greenhouse-gas emissions.
Road vehicles contributed 99.7 MtCO2e, or 90% of domestic transport emissions.
Cars and taxis contributed 59.5 MtCO2e; HGVs 18.4 MtCO2e; light vans 18.6 MtCO2e.
Domestic aviation contributed 1.2 MtCO2e and domestic shipping 4.0 MtCO2e.
National mode totals cannot be assigned to a road segment, facility or parcel without separate spatial allocation.

packages.title: DfT/DESNZ transport model and inventory-revision guard QA
facts: DfT transport greenhouse-gas data come from the DESNZ inventory and combine fuel-consumption with transport data in modelling.
The inventory is reviewed annually and historical values can be revised for methods, guidance or new data.
DfT reports an updated domestic-shipping method normalised to DUKES fuel-sold data.
International aviation and shipping are reported separately and excluded from the UK domestic total under the territorial convention.
2025 transport estimates are provisional and must not be treated as final detailed mode or parcel measurements.
